ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Small blocks A and B both have a mass of $m=0.10\mathsf{kg}$. Block B is initially at rest at the end of the horizontal section of the track. Block A collides with block B at a horizontal velocity $v_{0}$. After the collision, the two blocks stick together and are projected horizontally. The vertical height of the projection point above the horizontal ground is $h=0.45\mathrm{m}$, and the horizontal distance from the landing point of the two blocks to the end of the track is $s=0.30\mathrm{m}$. The acceleration due to gravity is taken as $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. Determine the time $t$ during which the two blocks are in projectile motion in the air.
2. Determine the magnitude of the velocity $v_{0}$ of block A before the collision.
3. Calculate the mechanical energy loss $\Delta E$ during the collision of the two blocks.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, small block A is located on the left inclined rail, moving along the rail toward the lower right; at the end of the right horizontal rail there is small block B. The position where B is located is above the ground, with the height labeled h; from the end of the rail toward the lower right, a dashed parabola is drawn, indicating that after the collision the two small blocks stuck together fly out horizontally and fall to the ground; the horizontal distance from the landing point to directly below the end of the rail is labeled s. Reasoning calculation: After the two blocks collide, they are projected horizontally, the initial velocity in the vertical direction is 0, and the vertical falling height is h=0.45 m, so h = (1/2)gt^2. Substituting g=10 m/s^2, t = sqrt(2h/g) = sqrt(2×0.45/10) = sqrt(0.09) = 0.30 s. In the horizontal direction there is uniform motion, and after the collision their common velocity is u = s/t = 0.30/0.30 = 1.0 m/s. During the collision process, momentum in the horizontal direction is conserved. Before the collision only A is moving, B is stationary, and the two blocks have the same mass, both m, therefore m v0 = (2m)u, obtaining v0 = 2u = 2.0 m/s. The loss of mechanical energy equals the kinetic energy before the collision minus the kinetic energy after the collision: ΔE = (1/2)m v0^2 - (1/2)(2m)u^2 = (1/2)(0.10)(2.0)^2 - (1/2)(0.20)(1.0)^2 = 0.20 - 0.10 = 0.10 J.
